exercises.name: Benchpress 45 incline
exercises.notes:
1. Setup and Starting Position: Sit at the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell resting vertically against each thigh. Carefully lean back while driving the dumbbells toward your chest with your knees.

2. The “Leg Drive” and Posture: Plant your feet firmly on the floor. Retract your shoulder blades (press them together against the bench) and maintain a slight natural lumbar curve.

3. Starting Position: Push the dumbbells toward the ceiling. Your wrists should be aligned with your elbows. Rotate the dumbbells slightly inward (about 45 degrees) so that your elbows do not splay out too far to the sides, thereby protecting your shoulders.

4. Eccentric Phase (Lowering): Lower the dumbbells in a controlled manner toward the sides of your chest. Your elbows should lower at an angle of about 45–60 degrees relative to your body. Feel the stretch in the lower part of your chest.

5. Concentric Phase (Lift): Push the weight upward in a slight arc (toward the center), without letting the dumbbells collide at the top or fully locking out your elbows to maintain muscle tension. Exhale as you lift.

exercises.name: Push-Ups, Decline
exercises.notes:
Decline push-ups are another modified version of the traditional push-up that target the upper body muscles in a different way. To perform a decline push-up, elevate your feet on an elevated surface, such as a bench, chair, or step, while placing your hands on the ground in a push-up position. Lower your body towards the ground while maintaining a straight line from your shoulders to your ankles, and then push back up to the starting position.
Unlike the inclined push-up, the decline push-up places more emphasis on the shoulders and triceps, while still engaging the chest muscles to a lesser extent. By elevating your feet, you increase the difficulty of the exercise by placing more weight on your upper body, forcing your shoulders and triceps to work harder to push your body back up. The decline push-up can be a great way to challenge your upper body strength and improve your ability to perform other push-up variations. As with any exercise, be sure to use proper form and start with a height that is appropriate for your strength and fitness level.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Extension
exercises.notes:
**Overhead Triceps Extension with EZ Bar – Quick Guide**

The **overhead position** *emphasizes the long head* of the triceps (because it's stretched under load), the exercise **does engage all three triceps heads** (long, lateral, and medial) to some degree during extension.

1. **Setup**:
   Sit on a bench (or stand) and hold an EZ bar with a narrow, overhand
   grip. Lift the bar overhead, arms fully extended. Keep your core tight
   and elbows close to your head.
2. **Execution**:
   Slowly lower the bar behind your head by bending your elbows until they
   reach ~90°. Keep elbows pointed forward (not flaring out).
3. **Finish**: Extend your arms back up to the starting position, squeezing your triceps at the top.

**Tips**:

* Control the movement to avoid straining your shoulders.
* Use a moderate weight for full range of motion.
* Keep your back straight and avoid arching.

* To **achieve new personal records** in your back squat, gradually increase weight over time, vary rep ranges and sets to stimulate muscle growth, and **prioritize rest and recovery** between training sessions.

exercises.notes:
The push-up is a fundamental bodyweight exercise that targets the chest, arms, and shoulders while engaging the core for stability. It requires no equipment and is excellent for building upper body strength.

Instructions:

1. Start in a plank position with hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width, feet together, and body in a straight line from head to heels.
2. Engage your core and lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body or flared slightly outward.
3. Lower until your chest nearly touches the ground while maintaining a neutral spine.
4. Push through your palms to return to the starting position, fully extending your arms.

exercises.notes: This exercise works the deltoid muscle of the shoulder. The movement starts with the arms straight, and the hands holding weights at the sides or in front of the body. Body is in a slight forward-leaning position with hips and knees bent a little. Arms are kept straight or slightly bent, and raised through an arc of movement in the coronal plane that terminates when the hands are at approximately shoulder height. Weights are lowered to the starting position, completing one rep. When using a cable machine the individual stands with the coronal plane in line with the pulley, which is at or near the ground.[9] The exercise can be completed one shoulder at a time (with the other hand used to stabilize the body against the weight moved), or with both hands simultaneously if two parallel pulleys are available.

exercises.name: Axe Hold
exercises.notes: Grab dumbbells and extend arms to side and hold as long as you can

exercises.name: Front Raises Alternated
exercises.notes:
To execute the exercise, the lifter stands with their feet shoulder width apart and weights or resistance handles held by their side with a pronated (overhand) grip.

The movement is to bring the arms up in front of the body to eye level and with only a slight bend in the elbow. This isolates the anterior deltoid muscle (front of the shoulder) and uses the anterior deltoid to lift the weight.

When lifting it is important to keep the body still so the anterior deltoid is fully utilised; if the weight cannot be lifted by standing still then it is too heavy and a lower weight is needed. It is important to keep a slight bend in the elbow when lifting as keeping the elbow locked will add stress to the elbow joint and could cause injury.

A neutral grip, similar to that used in the hammer curl, can also be used. With this variation the weight is again raised to eye level, but out to a 45 degree angle from the front of the body. This may be beneficial for those with shoulder injuries, particularly those related to the rotator cuff.

exercises.label: Abductor side plank with ball reach
exercises.name: Side Plank with Ball Push-Away Rotation
exercises.notes: Side plank on left elbow, left leg bent 90°, right leg straight on top. Ball under right hand, push it away while rotating the torso, extending the right arm until facing the floor.

exercises.label: Single leg goblet squat on bench
exercises.name: Single-Leg Goblet Squat to Bench
exercises.notes: Single-leg squat holding weight goblet-style at chest. Lower down until lightly touching a bench behind you, then stand back up.

exercises.name: Hyperextensions Hold
exercises.notes: Lie on the roman chair with your navel at the front edge, allowing your upper body to hang freely. Tighten all your back muscles and raise your torso until you're horizontal, but no higher. Lower yourself slowly, maintaining a steady flow of muscles.

exercises.name: Face pulls with resistance band
exercises.notes: Face pulls with band – standing horizontal pull. Grab the band at face height, pull elbows high and wide towards your face while squeezing shoulder blades together. Trains upper back, rear shoulders and improves posture.

exercises.name: Bicep curl to press
exercises.notes:
Bend your elbows and lift the dumbbells to your shoulders.
Push the dumbbells over your head while rotating your arms to make your palms face forward. Reverse it to lower down. Repeat the exercise.

exercises.label: Banded eccentric single leg slider hamstring curl
exercises.name: Banded Eccentric Single-Leg Slider Hamstring Curl
exercises.notes: Lying on back, one heel on a slider with band resistance. Slowly extend the leg out, then curl it back in.

exercises.name: Bench Press Narrow Grip
exercises.notes:
- **Setup:** Lie flat on the bench and grip the bar at shoulder-width (closer than a standard bench press).
- **Descent:** Lower the bar with control to your lower chest.
- **Form:** Keep your elbows tucked in tight against your torso—do not let them flare out.
- **Ascent:** Press the bar straight back up, squeezing your triceps at the top.

exercises.name: Pistol Squat
exercises.notes:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, toes pointed forward, and chest tall.
2. Extend your leg straight out; extend both arms in front of you, at shoulder level. Brace your core and look straight ahead.
3. Slowly squat down.
4. (optional) pause at the bottom.

Keep your (free) leg and arms extended for the whole duration.

exercises.label: "reverse Fly" triceps
exercises.name: Incline Lying Triceps Extension
exercises.notes: Face-down on incline bench. Bend elbows, extend arms fully.

exercises.name: Loaded Split Stance Hip Rotation
exercises.notes: stance holding a kettlebell. Rotate the hips.

exercises.name: Reverse Grip Ezbar Curls
exercises.notes:
Hold the barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down) approximately shoulder-width apart. Ensure your back is straight, shoulders slightly pulled back, and arms fully extended.
Curl the barbell upwards towards your chest in a controlled motion, keeping your elbows close to your body. The motion should be smooth without any swinging or momentum use.
Once the barbell is at chest level, pause briefly to maximize contraction in the biceps and forearms.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with a controlled movement, fully extending your arms.

exercises.label: Trx bridge
exercises.name: TRX Hip Bridge Curl
exercises.notes: Feet in TRX straps, lift hips into bridge, curl feet in toward body.

exercises.name: Suspended Archer Push Ups
exercises.notes: Suspension exercise with trx for chest training

exercises.name: Preacher curl, Ez Bar
exercises.notes: Roman chair, curl one dumbbell at a time.

exercises.name: Archer Pull-ups
exercises.notes: Grab the pull up bar with a wide grip, the body is hanging freely. Keep your chest out and pull yourself up till your chin reaches the bar or it touches your neck, if you want to pull behind you. Go with a slow and controlled movement down, always keeping the chest out.

exercises.name: Flat Leg Crunch
exercises.notes: Legs straight and relaxed on floor. Short-range crunch, upper abs focus.

exercises.name: Fire Hydrant Extension Hold
exercises.notes: All fours, lift bent knee to side, extend leg straight, rHold

exercises.name: Shrug Rolling Forward
exercises.notes: Dumbbell each hand, shrug up, rotate Forward.

exercises.name: bicep curls, wide
exercises.notes:
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and palms facing forward.
Bend your elbows and lift the dumbbells to your shoulders. Slowly return and repeat.

exercises.name: Lunge Outward Pull
exercises.notes: Lunge with band around front leg, pulling inward.

exercises.label: Bench glute stretch with contralateral row (with resistance band)
exercises.name: Bench Glute Stretch with Contralateral Row
exercises.notes: One leg stretched on a bench in a glute stretch position. Row with the band using the opposite-side arm.

exercises.label: lower back crunch arms backward
exercises.name: Prone Extension with Arm Reach
exercises.notes: Lying face-down, lift torso, then extend arms backward.

exercises.name: Lunge Outward Pull, Hold
exercises.notes: Lunge with band around front leg, pulling inward.

exercises.name: Bent Over Rowing Reverse grip
exercises.notes:
The same as *regular* rowing, but holding a reversed grip (your palms pointing forwards):

Grab the barbell with a wide grIp (slightly more than shoulder wide) and lean forward. Your upper body is not quite parallel to the floor, but forms a slight angle. The chest's out during the whole exercise.

Pull now the barbell with a fast movement towards your belly button, not further up. Go slowly down to the initial position. Don't swing with your body and keep your arms next to your body.

exercises.label: Abductor lounge with resistance band
exercises.name: Resistance Band Abductor Lunge
exercises.notes: Lunge with a resistance band around the legs, engaging the hip abductors.

exercises.label: lower back crunch arms backward - Hold
exercises.name: Prone Extension with Arm Reach, Hold
exercises.notes: Lying face-down, lift torso, then extend arms backward.

exercises.label: Band Chop w Outside Knee on Bench
exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Band Wood Chop (Outside Knee on Bench)
exercises.notes: Half-kneeling with the outside knee up on a bench. Perform a diagonal chopping motion with the band.

exercises.name: Chin Up
exercises.notes: The chin-up (also known as a chin or chinup) is a strength training exercise. People frequently do this exercise with the intention of strengthening muscles such as the latissimus dorsi and biceps, which extend the shoulder and flex the elbow, respectively. In this maneuver, the palms are faced towards the body. It is a form of pull-up in which the range of motion is established in relation to a person's chin.

exercises.name: Shrugs
exercises.notes:
Stand with straight body, the hands are hanging freely on the side and hold each a dumbbell. Lift from this position the shoulders as high as you can, but don't bend the arms during the movement. On the highest point, make a short pause of 1 or 2 seconds before returning slowly to the initial position.

When training with a higher weight, make sure that you still do the whole movement!

exercises.name: Donkey Kick bent knee, Hold
exercises.notes: All fours, knee bent, kick leg straight pulse up and down.

exercises.name: V ups
exercises.notes: Using a medicine ball as an overload will make the exercise heavier.

exercises.name: Figure-4
exercises.notes: One leg bent in figure-4, other leg straight. raise straight leg

exercises.name: Crunch W Straight Leg Raised, Pulse
exercises.notes: Legs straight, raised toward ceiling. Small, fast pulses at top.

exercises.name: Bar Dips
exercises.notes: A dip is an upper-body strength exercise. Narrow, shoulder-width dips primarily train the triceps, with major synergists being the anterior deltoid, the pectoralis muscles (sternal, clavicular, and minor), and the rhomboid muscles of the back (in that order).[1] Wide arm training places additional emphasis on the pectoral muscles, similar in respect to the way a wide grip bench press would focus more on the pectorals and less on the triceps.

exercises.name: Active Hip Flexor to Hamstring Stretch
exercises.notes: Half-kneeling lunge position. Rock forward for a hip flexor stretch, then rock back for a hamstring stretch.

exercises.name: Hammer curl Alternated
exercises.notes: Stand with your knees slightly bent and your back straight. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, using a neutral grip at your sides.

exercises.name: Donkey Kick bent knee
exercises.notes: All fours, knee bent, kick leg straight pulse up and down, with option of dumbell between knee

exercises.name: Plank Shoulder Taps
exercises.notes: In the correct plank position, place your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. alternately lift and touch the opposite shoulder with one hand.

exercises.name: Biceps with TRX
exercises.notes: Grab the handles of the TRX straps, lean your body back, arms and legs extended, with your body positioned in a single straight line. (This is an arm exercise, not an abdominal one.)

exercises.name: Crunch W Straight Leg Raised
exercises.notes: Legs straight, raised toward ceiling. Crunch toward feet.

exercises.label: Reverse clamshell, using something between knee
exercises.name: Reverse Clamshell (Object Between Knees)
exercises.notes: Side-lying, knees bent with an object held between them. Lift ankles apart, keeping knees together.

exercises.label: glutes kickback
exercises.name: Kneeling kickbacks
exercises.notes:
Starting position:

Get down on all fours.

Steps:

1. Push one foot back until fully extended, concentrating on the gluteus muscles.
2. Stay for one second, then return to the initial position.
3. Repeat, alternating feet.

exercises.name: Chest Fly
exercises.notes: Take two dumbbells and lay on a bench, make sure the feet are firmly on the ground and your back is not arched, but has good contact with the bench. The arms are stretched in front of you, about shoulder wide. Bend now the arms a bit and let them down with a half-circle movement to the side. Without changing the angle of the elbow bring them in a fluid movement back up.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.notes:
Get into a position on the floor supporting your weight on your forearms and toes. Arms are bent and directly below the shoulder.

Keep your body straight at all times and hold this position as long as possible. To increase difficulty an arm or leg can be raised while performing this exercise.

exercises.name: Hyperextensions One leg
exercises.notes: Lie on the roman chair with your navel at the front edge, allowing your upper body to hang freely. Tighten all your back muscles and raise your torso until you're horizontal, but no higher. Lower yourself slowly, maintaining a steady flow of muscles.

exercises.label: Biceps Curls Reverse grip
exercises.name: Biceps Curls With reverse grip
exercises.notes: Reverse grip bicep curl

exercises.name: Crunch W Straight Leg Raised, Hold
exercises.notes: Legs straight, raised toward ceiling. Hold at top.

exercises.name: Preacher Curl, DB
exercises.notes: Roman chair, curl one dumbbell at a time.

exercises.name: Lunge Inward Pull, Hold
exercises.notes: Lunge with band around front leg, pulling inward.

exercises.name: Lunge Outward Pull, Pulse
exercises.notes: Lunge with band around front leg, pulling inward.

exercises.label: bench glute stretch w contralateral row
exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Cross-Body Rotational Row with Contralateral Glute Stretch
exercises.notes: Half-kneeling position, stretching the opposite-side glute, while performing a rotational cross-body row.

exercises.name: Trap press
exercises.notes: Laying flat with arm pointing straight upwards, elbow fully extended, use only your shoulder to raise the weight as high as comfortable and back to rest.

exercises.name: Bus Drivers
exercises.notes: Sitting with a Weight Plate, used as wheel, in both hands; raised slightly below eye level

exercises.label: Hanging Straight Leg Raise
exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.notes: Hang from bar, raise a straight leg in front.

exercises.label: 1db press sit
exercises.name: Seated Overhead Triceps Extension 1DB
exercises.notes: Seated, one dumbbell held with both hands overhead, lower behind head, press up.

exercises.name: Upright Row
exercises.notes: Hold a dumbbell in each hand in front of your body. Keep your palms towards your body. Lift you hands straight up until your hands are under your chin, then lower them. Repeat the exercise.

exercises.name: Hyperextensions Rounded spine
exercises.notes: Rounded spine when going up and down to full extension

exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch
exercises.notes: Pedal legs, opposite elbow to opposite knee, alternating.

exercises.name: Ab Crunch, pulse
exercises.notes: Knees bent, feet flat. Crunch shoulders toward knees.

exercises.label: lower back crunch, Pulse
exercises.name: Prone Back Extension, Pulse
exercises.notes: Lying face-down, lift torso up and down using lower back.

exercises.name: Suspended Push Ups
exercises.notes: Suspension exercise with trx for chest training

exercises.name: Fire Hydrant, Pulse
exercises.notes: All fours, knee bent, lift leg out to the side. pulse movement on top

exercises.name: Push Up
exercises.notes:
The push-up is a fundamental bodyweight exercise that targets the chest, arms, and shoulders while engaging the core for stability. It requires no equipment and is excellent for building upper body strength.

Instructions:

1. Start in a plank position with hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width, feet together, and body in a straight line from head to heels.
2. Engage your core and lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body or flared slightly outward.
3. Lower until your chest nearly touches the ground while maintaining a neutral spine.
4. Push through your palms to return to the starting position, fully extending your arms.

exercises.name: Lunges
exercises.notes: This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in each hand and stepping back into a lunge position, then returning to standing. It primarily targets the glutes, hamstrings, and quadriceps.

exercises.name: Bent Over Rowing
exercises.notes:
1. Holding a barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing down), bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward, by bending at the waist, while keeping the back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor. Tip: Make sure that you keep the head up. The barbell should hang directly in front of you as your arms hang perpendicular to the floor and your torso. This is your starting position.
2. Now, while keeping the torso stationary, breathe out and lift the barbell to you. Keep the elbows close to the body and only use the forearms to hold the weight. At the top contracted position, squeeze the back muscles and hold for a brief pause.
3. Then inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
4. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.label: Hip thrust
exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.notes: Also doable 1 or 2 dumbells

exercises.name: Side Bend, DB
exercises.notes: This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in one hand and bending sideways to work the oblique muscles on the side of the body. It can be done standing or seated and is often used as a core strengthening exercise.

exercises.name: Triceps Kickback (3-Point Stance)
exercises.notes: One hand on bench, dumbbell in other hand. Push weight back with triceps.

exercises.name: Standing DB Hip Flexion
exercises.notes: Standing, holding a kettlebell, raise the knee up against resistance.

exercises.name: Lateral Push Off
exercises.notes: Push off the ground and land on one leg and regain balance before jumping to the other leg

exercises.name: Dumbbell Wrist Curl
exercises.notes:
Sitting on a bench, grab a dumbell with your palms facing up and your hands shoulder-width apart. Rest your forearms on your thighs and allow your wrists to hang over your knees. Perform the movement by curling your palms and wrists towards your face.

Pause for a moment in the top position, then slowly return the barbell to the starting position.

exercises.name: Flat Leg Crunch, Pulse
exercises.notes: Legs straight and relaxed on floor. Short-range crunch, upper abs focus.

exercises.name: 90° Rotational Lunge to Box Step-Up
exercises.notes: From a lunge position, rotate the body 90° and step one leg onto a raised box while holding a weight plate overhead.
